name: Jimp
role: Pure-JavaScript image manipulation, no native dependencies; slow but trivially portable
summary: Node image library written entirely in JavaScript with zero native dependencies, driven from code: read, resize, crop, composite, filter, write PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF. Strength is install-anywhere portability, including sandboxes where native binaries fail. Cost is speed and memory, since all pixel work runs in JS.
use_when: Over Sharp when native binaries cannot install (restricted CI, edge runtimes)
Small tweaks on a handful of frames where startup cost dominates
Per-pixel JS callbacks over a bitmap with no extra tooling
avoid_when: Batches or large images: Sharp is several times faster
Format breadth (AVIF, WebP, SVG, ICC): Sharp or ImageMagick
Shell scripts with no Node project: ImageMagick
Pure pixel access in the browser: Image.js or canvas-2d
notes: 2026-10-26: npm jimp 1.6.1 published 2026-04-07 and the last repository push was the same day; roughly six months since a release, inside the active window. Speed comparison with Sharp is from general knowledge, not measured.

assessment.rationale: npm latest 1.6.1 published 2026-04-07, last repo push the same day. Pure-JS niche is real, but Sharp wins on speed and format coverage wherever native install works.
